title: A restore that leaves out damaged workouts still says it restored everything, and after Replace those workouts are gone from the phone
what: Restore from a backup file first shows 'In this backup: 50 workouts'. Any workout in the file that cannot be read is quietly left out while the restore runs; the count of left-out items is worked out but never shown. The member then reads 'Restored 48 workouts' with no word about the 2 missing. After 'Replace everything on this phone', the phone's own copy of those workouts was already deleted, so they exist only in the file and the member has no reason to look.
expected: The finished line says how many workouts could not be read and were left out, so the numbers before and after match, and the member knows to keep the file.
how_often: rare: only when a backup file holds a damaged or unreadable workout
fix_line: Add the left-out count to the 'Restored' line

title: Changing your mobile number in Edit profile never reaches your gym, though the screen says your gym will use it
what: Under the mobile number box the app says the number stays on the phone and 'only your gym will use it, once you link one'. The number is saved only on the phone. Joining a gym by code or poster does not send it, and changing it later is never sent to the gym. Only 'Find my gym' reads it, once. So a member who changes number here believes the gym now has the new one, while the gym's reminders and receipts keep going to the old number.
expected: Either a changed number is offered to the linked gym (with the member's yes), or the line says plainly that the gym keeps its own copy and the member should tell the desk.
who: gym members who change their mobile number
how_often: every time a joined member changes the number
fix_line: Reword the line to say the gym keeps its own copy, or send the change to the gym after asking

title: A quick double tap on Save my history or Save my measurements makes the file twice and opens two share sheets
what: These two buttons stop a second tap only by a screen flag that is not yet set when a fast second tap arrives, so both taps start a save. The member gets two share sheets one after the other and may save two copies. The backup file and restore buttons in this area use a guard that a double tap cannot slip past.
expected: A second tap while the first save runs does nothing, as on Save the backup file.
fix_line: Use the same instant guard the backup file button uses
